prior_block:
PRICE PRIORS for recurring line types (statistical model fitted on the thresholds t revealed
in earlier games; gross amounts). How to use them:
- The amounts are final thresholds as they were revealed: they already contain whatever
  deductible, VAT and customary-price judgement applied in those cases, and they were computed
  from the full invoiced quantity (the whole quantity was indemnified there). For an
  indemnified line of this type take the stated amount for the line as t as it stands and give
  a price_log_sd that matches the stated range. Do not deduct a deductible from it and do not
  cut the invoiced quantity.
- Deviate only for something this case has and those cases did not: an aggregate cap or
  sub-limit that the lines of this invoice must share, a percentage reduction for a breached
  duty, or a purchase price or sum insured stated in the claim that limits the line.
- Whether a line is indemnified in THIS case is decided by the policy and the claim, not by
  the history. The history only says how often this line type was paid at all. A line type
  that was never indemnified before is usually an ancillary charge the policies do not carry;
  treat it as indemnified only if this policy clearly says so.
- line 2 "Vehicle costs": indemnified in 9 of 19 earlier cases, t = 0 in 10; when indemnified t per pc about 79 (80% range 71 to 87); revealed per pc: 38-44 (case 25*), >=68 (case 18), >=76 (case 21), >=76 (case 21), >=76 (case 21), >=74 (case 27) (* = other policy wording)
- line 10 "Vehicle costs": indemnified in 9 of 19 earlier cases, t = 0 in 10; when indemnified t per pc about 79 (80% range 71 to 87); revealed per pc: 38-44 (case 25*), >=68 (case 18), >=76 (case 21), >=76 (case 21), >=76 (case 21), >=74 (case 27) (* = other policy wording)

items.description: Electrician labour checking and rewiring the flooded basement circuits
items.rationale: The policy only covers damage caused by an insured peril. Here, the flooding was caused by surface water/rainwater ingress (inundation), not by escape of water from insured pipework (see 2.4, 2.5, 3.6). The schedule does not record the further natural hazards group (c2), so inundation is not insured. Per 3.6.2, no indemnity arises for any repair, labour or material.

Journey/vehicle charges are only indemnified if the underlying work is covered (7.1.7(g)), and are barred entirely if the claim is excluded by 3.6. Here, the cause is inundation, which is not insured, so 3.6.2(f) applies: t = 0.
Working equipment (1.3, 4.3(d), 7.1.8(b)) is not insured property and is not indemnified, especially when the claim as a whole is barred by 3.6 (inundation, not an insured peril).
As above, working equipment is not insured property (1.3, 4.3(d)), and the claim is barred by 3.6 due to inundation. No indemnity.

items.description: Water extraction from the flooded basement
items.rationale: Measures to remove standing water are only covered if the peril is insured and the cause is established (5.2.2, 3.6). Here, inundation is not insured, so 3.6.2(d) applies: t = 0.

items.description: Small electrical materials for the rewiring
items.rationale: Materials for repair are only indemnified if the underlying damage is covered. Here, the cause is inundation, which is not insured (3.6.2(c)), so t = 0.

items.description: Renew boiler system including flue gas system and storage tank
items.rationale: The boiler was damaged by inundation (surface water/rainwater), not by an insured peril (2.4, 2.5, 3.6). The schedule does not record the further natural hazards group (c2), so no indemnity for repair or replacement of plant (3.6.2(a)).

items.description: Adjust supply pipework to fit the replacement boiler
items.rationale: Ancillary work to fit the new boiler is only covered if the main replacement is covered. Here, the claim is barred by 3.6 (inundation), so t = 0.

items.description: Dispose of the old boiler system
items.rationale: Disposal of damaged property is only covered if the damage is caused by an insured peril. Here, inundation is not insured (3.6.2(e)), so t = 0.

Journey/vehicle charges are only indemnified if the underlying work is covered (7.1.7(g)), and are barred entirely if the claim is excluded by 3.6. Here, the cause is inundation, which is not insured, so 3.6.2(f) applies: t = 0.
